punchline: A librarian in Alexandria worked out the size of the Earth from a stick and its shadow.
thirty_sec: In Carl Sagan's Cosmos, Eratosthenes, head of the library at Alexandria, reads that at Syene a stick casts no shadow at noon on the summer solstice. In Alexandria, the same kind of stick does. The gap shows the two cities sit about one fiftieth of a circle apart. He has a man pace out about 800 kilometres, multiplies by 50, and gets about 40,000 kilometres, within a few percent of the truth by Sagan's account.
